dsa5208-orientation.title: Distributed experiment evidence map
dsa5208-orientation.learningGoal: Connect a distributed claim to its system conditions and measurements.

sourceLens.whyExaminable: The overview turns scale, failure, communication, and coordination into the evidence vocabulary for later project work.

nodes.label: Claim
nodes.detail: What the system is supposed to achieve.

dsa5208-orientation.explanation: A distributed experiment is a chain from claim to setting to metric to evidence; the final result is not meaningful without the earlier context.

dsa5208-distributed-models.title: Process and event-history map
dsa5208-distributed-models.learningGoal: Separate processes, local histories, messages, and the global event set.

sourceLens.whyExaminable: The process/event model is the assumption boundary for every causal-ordering derivation.

nodes.label: Process
nodes.detail: An independent entity with local state.

nodes.label: Global event set
nodes.detail: The union of all local histories.

dsa5208-distributed-models.explanation: The map keeps local state and cross-process communication distinct before causal edges are derived.

dsa5208-happens-before.title: Causal-edge checker
dsa5208-happens-before.learningGoal: Choose the rule that justifies a proposed happens-before edge.

sourceLens.whyExaminable: Happens-before is the formal bridge from a message-passing diagram to clocks and delivery guarantees.

reference.sourceId: L. Lamport, Time, Clocks, and the Ordering of Events in a Distributed System

splits.label: No edge
splits.detail: Check the reverse direction before calling events concurrent.

dsa5208-happens-before.explanation: The checker forces the learner to justify an edge with a model rule rather than visual intuition.

dsa5208-communication-ordering.title: Delivery-guarantee explorer
dsa5208-communication-ordering.learningGoal: Choose the weakest delivery guarantee that preserves an application invariant.

sourceLens.whyExaminable: Delivery guarantees are a compact distinction between channel-local order and system-wide causal order.

dsa5208-communication-ordering.invariant: A process broadcasts an update after observing a causally earlier update; every receiver must deliver the earlier update first.

splits.label: Best effort
splits.detail: May deliver messages in arbitrary order; it cannot preserve the causal dependency.

splits.label: FIFO channel
splits.detail: Preserves one sender's broadcast sequence, but not a dependency crossing processes.

splits.label: Causal delivery
splits.detail: Preserves the observed-before-broadcast dependency without forcing one order on concurrent messages.

splits.label: Total order
splits.detail: Also orders concurrent messages globally, which is stronger than this invariant requires.

dsa5208-communication-ordering.incorrectChoiceMessage: That guarantee does not preserve the stated invariant
dsa5208-communication-ordering.explanation: Move toward stronger guarantees only when the application invariant needs more than arbitrary or per-channel delivery order.

dsa5208-physical-clocks.title: NTP delay trace
dsa5208-physical-clocks.learningGoal: Trace the four timestamps into a delay estimate and state its assumptions.

sourceLens.whyExaminable: NTP is a concrete calculation checkpoint and a clean contrast with causal logical time.

steps: Identify client and server send/receive timestamps.
dsa5208-physical-clocks.explanation: The trace separates arithmetic from the assumptions needed to interpret an NTP estimate.

dsa5208-lamport-scalar.title: Lamport scalar trace
dsa5208-lamport-scalar.learningGoal: Apply local, send, and receive updates in the correct order.

sourceLens.whyExaminable: Scalar clocks are a core derivation because every later ordering claim depends on the receive max-and-increment rule.

reference.sourceId: L. Lamport, Time, Clocks, and the Ordering of Events in a Distributed System

steps: Advance before a send or internal event.
Place the receive event strictly after both histories.
dsa5208-lamport-scalar.explanation: The trace makes the one-way causal guarantee and the receive-event ordering visible.

dsa5208-vector-clocks.title: Vector comparison trace
dsa5208-vector-clocks.learningGoal: Compare every component and identify causal order versus concurrency.

sourceLens.whyExaminable: Vector clocks extend scalar time with enough process-specific state to recover concurrency.

reference.sourceId: L. Lamport, Time, Clocks, and the Ordering of Events in a Distributed System

steps: Check no component is larger and one is strictly smaller.
dsa5208-vector-clocks.explanation: The learner must use componentwise comparison rather than a scalar or lexicographic shortcut.

dsa5208-compressed-timestamps.title: Timestamp-storage explorer
dsa5208-compressed-timestamps.learningGoal: Compare full vectors, receiver-specific deltas, and differential metadata state.

sourceLens.whyExaminable: This lab turns a complexity statement into a design trade-off: preserve causal knowledge while reducing repeated metadata.

options.label: Full vector
options.detail: Stores one counter per process, making comparison direct while metadata grows with the process count.

options.label: Receiver-specific delta
options.detail: Sends only counters changed since the receiver's baseline, but both sides must maintain compatible state.

options.label: Differential metadata
options.detail: Reuses a prior metadata state and transmits increments; decoding depends on a valid base state.

dsa5208-compressed-timestamps.explanation: More compression can reduce communication and storage, but it requires carefully maintained receiver-specific state.

dsa5208-consistency-spark.title: Consistency diagnosis studio
dsa5208-consistency-spark.learningGoal: Classify a consistency history, separate a session guarantee from majority commitment, and trace digest read repair.

sourceLens.whyExaminable: Lecture 3 is easiest to confuse when a history, a client session, and a replica repair path are treated as the same guarantee. Each panel isolates one proof obligation.

exercises.label: Data-centric history
exercises.prompt: Which guarantee does this history require?
steps: Mark the causal edge before judging the read order.
The observer saw the effect before its cause.
This observation violates causal consistency and any stronger model.
Do not impose a total order on writes that are truly concurrent.

sourceLens.whyExaminable: Causal consistency preserves related writes without requiring one global order for concurrent writes.

exercises.takeaway: A history must be judged against its causal edges before a stronger real-time or global-order claim is made.

exercises.label: Read-your-writes
exercises.prompt: Why can majority acknowledgement still need session state?
steps: The write is committed by the configured write concern.
A serving node may still lag this client's latest write.
The session carries the required ordering point until the node catches up.
Separate majority commitment from client-visible session ordering.

sourceLens.whyExaminable: The lecture separates a replica's majority state from the guarantee that one client sees its own completed write.

exercises.takeaway: A write concern describes commitment; a session guarantee describes what this client's later read must observe.

exercises.label: Digest read repair
exercises.prompt: What happens after two replica digests disagree?
steps: A compact digest mismatch signals divergent replica versions.
The coordinator requests complete values only after the mismatch.
Resolve the version to return to the client.
Read repair reduces future divergence after the response.

sourceLens.whyExaminable: Digest reads save traffic when replicas agree, while mismatch activates reconciliation and repair.

exercises.takeaway: A digest is an agreement test, not the final value; disagreement opens the full-read and repair path.

dsa5208-consistency-spark.explanation: Use one panel for each reasoning boundary: classify the history, enforce the client's session view, and repair divergent replicas.

dsa5208-broadcast.title: Broadcast guarantee selector
dsa5208-broadcast.learningGoal: Choose the weakest broadcast guarantee that preserves the application's ordering invariant.

sourceLens.whyExaminable: Lecture 2 makes the scope boundary examinable: FIFO is sender-channel local, causal order follows happens-before, and total order is global.

dsa5208-broadcast.invariant: If a process broadcasts an update after observing an earlier update, every process must deliver the earlier update first; concurrent broadcasts need not share one global position.

splits.label: FIFO broadcast
splits.detail: Preserves the order of messages broadcast by one process, but not dependencies crossing processes.

splits.label: Causal broadcast
splits.detail: Preserves dependencies between broadcasts without imposing one order on concurrent messages.

splits.label: Total-order broadcast
splits.detail: Makes every process deliver all messages in one common order, including concurrent messages.

splits.label: FIFO-total order
splits.detail: Adds each sender's FIFO order to a common global order; it is stronger than the stated invariant.

dsa5208-broadcast.incorrectChoiceMessage: That guarantee does not preserve the stated invariant
dsa5208-broadcast.explanation: The selector forces the learner to name the dependency scope before choosing a delivery protocol.

dsa5208-shortest-path.title: Distributed Bellman–Ford trace
dsa5208-shortest-path.learningGoal: Trace one distance relaxation and decide whether the execution is round-based or event-driven.

sourceLens.whyExaminable: The lab turns the lecture's main distinction into a decision: fixed rounds and a global barrier versus improvement-triggered messages and explicit termination.

steps: Set the source distance and leave unknown paths infinite.
Use a neighbor's known path plus edge latency.
Synchronous execution waits for a round; asynchronous execution reacts to an improvement.
$n-1$ rounds or no update in flight
Termination is part of the distributed algorithm, not an afterthought.
dsa5208-shortest-path.explanation: The trace keeps the shortest-path recurrence separate from the execution model that transports it.

dsa5208-synchronizers.title: Synchronizer round barrier
dsa5208-synchronizers.learningGoal: Decide when a process is safe to advance a simulated synchronous round.

sourceLens.whyExaminable: A synchronizer is the correctness bridge between asynchronous execution and a synchronous algorithm; safe progress is the key invariant.

steps: Name the round whose messages are being processed.
Track messages from neighbors for this round.
Wait for the protocol's evidence that the round is complete.
Only then run the next synchronous step safely.
dsa5208-synchronizers.explanation: The timeline makes a logical barrier visible without pretending the physical network has a global clock.
